_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Hyundai Motor India (consolidated, Rs crore; subsidiaries are tiny: an engineering-services company and an insurance broker). Revenue = vehicles sold (domestic + exports, company wholesale basis) x revenue per vehicle (all operating revenue incl. parts, engineering services, export incentives and government scheme income, divided by vehicles). The domestic / export build is in `build` and is checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/HYUNDAI.ctx.js. FY26 base: 775,031 vehicles (584,906 domestic + 190,125 exports), revenue Rs70,763 cr, Rs913,033 per vehicle. Screener's Net Profit equals Profit for EPS (no minorities), so no patchRaw. Shares 81.25 cr (IPO in Oct-2024 was a pure offer for sale: no new shares). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS as the street does.

volume._why: Company wholesale volumes (domestic + exports). FY27E 827,673 (+6.8%): domestic +9% (guidance 8-10%; Apr-Aug +12.6% to 247,980; Sep-Mar must grow ~7% against the GST-boosted base, helped by the Bayon mid-SUV from Oct-2026, the localised compact EV in H2 and the Pune third shift from Oct-2026; management expects the industry to grow only in low single digits in H2) and exports flat at 190,125 (guidance 8-10%, but Apr-Aug was -11.7%: Q1 -19.6% on the West Asia conflict and the June supplier fire, July +31%, August -31% on shipping constraints). FY28E +9.9% (domestic +10%: full year of two new nameplates, Chennai Plant 1 utilisation 72% to ~90% in CY27, Pune Phase 2 by CY28; exports +10% from a low base: new Venue global sourcing, Exter LHD, Verna PE, EV and Bayon exports). FY29E +8% (both). Capacity 994k at Mar-26 (Chennai 824k + Pune 170k), 1.07 mn after Pune Phase 2 (CY28), >1.1 mn by 2030: FY29E volume is ~92% of the CY28 capacity. Brokers: MOSL ~9% volume CAGR FY26-28E; Nirmal Bang 9.3%; JM domestic 8.5%/8.2%, exports 10%/12%.

_revPerUnitWhy: Revenue per vehicle = revenue from operations / wholesale volume: Rs897,690 (FY24), Rs907,982 (FY25), Rs913,038 (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs917,251 (+0.8% YoY, +2.1% QoQ; JM). FY27E +2.5%: three price rises in CY26 (~100bp cumulative), lower discounts (2.8% of ASP in Q1FY27 vs 3.4%), Bayon (above Venue) and the EV (priced above ICE equivalents) in H2, rupee weakness on export ASPs (export ASP +7% YoY in Q1). FY28E +3%: full-year mix of two new SUVs and the EV. FY29E +2.5%: price ~1.5% plus mix. Parts revenue fell in FY26 (Rs3,392 cr vs Rs4,306 cr) and is a drag we do not try to forecast separately.
_marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income): 12.5% FY23, 13.0% FY24, 12.9% FY25, 12.1% FY26, 9.3% in Q1FY27 (supplier fire cost ~13,900 vehicles, mostly Creta; exports -20%; commodity hit ~100bp QoQ and ~200bp YoY in precious metals and copper; Pune stabilisation costs; employee cost +20%). Guidance: 11-14% for FY27, reiterated on 30-Jul-2026. FY27E 11.0% = Q1 9.3% plus ~11.5% for Q2-Q4 (volume recovery, price rises, no launch discounts on new models) - the bottom of the range, because commodity pressure is not over and the EV and Bayon launches carry marketing and start-up costs. FY28E 12.3%: Chennai Plant 1 utilisation back to ~90%, operating leverage on the Pune plant, localisation 83% to 90% by 2030. FY29E 12.8%, still below FY24-25 (~13%): royalty (2.8% of revenue), EV mix and competition (M&M, Tata, Maruti, Kia in SUVs). Street FY27E 11.0% (Nirmal Bang) to 12.1% (BOB Caps); FY28E 11.4% to 13.3%; Nomura 11.5% / 12.7% / 13.4%.
_capexWhy: FY27 capex guided at ~Rs7,500 cr, 'the highest ever' (Q4FY26 call, 8-May-2026): mainly Pune Phase 2 (170k to 250k by CY28) and Chennai upgrades, plus the two FY27 launches. The company plans to invest Rs45,000 cr over FY26-FY30 in capacity, electrification and 26 new products and variants (AR FY26); Screener capex FY26 Rs4,266 cr. Pune Phase 3 (+70k to ~320k by 2030) follows. We model Rs8,500 cr a year for FY28-29E; spending the full Rs45,000 cr plan would mean ~Rs11,000 cr a year in FY28-30, a downside risk to free cash flow.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs2,198 cr = 7.7% of average gross block (Rs28,692 cr), but gross block jumped by Rs7,997 cr when the Pune plant was capitalised in H2FY26. Q1FY27 depreciation Rs557 cr (Rs2,228 cr annualised). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs725 cr) and depreciates capex at once, although much of the Rs7,500-8,500 cr a year will sit in CWIP until Pune Phase 2 starts; 6.2% gives Rs2,259 cr in FY27E, Rs2,755 cr in FY28E and Rs3,282 cr in FY29E (3.4% of revenue vs 3.0-3.2% in FY24-26).
_treasuryWhy: Treasury = cash and bank deposits (Rs10,552 cr at Mar-26) less borrowings (Rs1,098 cr incl. leases) = Rs9,461 cr. FY26 interest income Rs547 cr (fixed deposits Rs455 cr, tax refunds Rs14 cr, others Rs76 cr; AR FY26 consolidated note 30) on average gross cash of Rs9,566 cr = 5.7%; on average net cash (~Rs8,600 cr) ~6.4%. FY25: Rs616 cr. Deposit rates fell in 2025-26, so 5.8% on net treasury.
_otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: royalty received Rs120 cr (FY26), rental income Rs49 cr, other non-operating income Rs92 cr and profit on asset sales Rs7 cr = ~Rs270 cr in FY26, growing with the business; plus a small allowance for exchange gains. FY26 reported other income Rs949 cr (AR note 30) = interest Rs547 cr + royalty Rs120 cr + exchange gain Rs133 cr + rental Rs49 cr + other Rs100 cr; Screener shows Rs986 cr (including Rs4 cr of exceptional items and classification differences). TTM to Jun-26 Rs1,001 cr. We do not forecast most exchange gains (Rs133 cr in FY26, Rs13 cr in FY25), so FY27E other income (~Rs800 cr) is below FY26.
_interestLabel: Interest cost (SIPCOT soft loan, leases, working-capital lines)
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs106 cr; Q1FY27 Rs27 cr. Borrowings Rs1,098 cr at Mar-26 (long-term Rs455 cr, mainly the Tamil Nadu sales-tax soft loan; short-term Rs542 cr; leases Rs101 cr), repaid over time.
_taxWhy: Effective tax 25.9% in FY25 and FY26 (statutory 25.17% plus disallowances such as CSR); Q1FY27 26.0%.
_payoutWhy: Dividend Rs21 a share for FY25 and FY26 (30% and 31.4% of EPS). The revised dividend policy (Oct-2025) sets no fixed payout. FY24 included ~Rs15,400 cr of dividends paid to HMC before the IPO (derived from the fall in reserves), which we do not expect to repeat while capex is Rs7,500-8,500 cr a year.

build._note: Domestic / export build (company wholesale volumes). Revenue per vehicle is one blended figure; the split of revenue by geography (AR FY26 note 29: domestic vehicles Rs45,150 cr, exported vehicles Rs15,598 cr; parts Rs3,392 cr; services Rs5,251 cr; other operating revenue Rs1,372 cr) is shown in the report but not modelled separately. Checked against model volume in HYUNDAI.ctx.js.
build._why: Domestic: guidance 8-10% (Apr-Aug +12.6%). Exports: guidance 8-10% but Apr-Aug -11.7% on the West Asia conflict; we assume flat for FY27E, then recovery.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash; cyclical but large, diversified PV maker with an export arm; cost of equity 11.9%.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; PV penetration is low (~30 cars per 1,000 people), but Hyundai is losing share and pays a royalty for its technology. 5.5%, the middle of the house 5-6% range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% over 15 years: volume ~4-5% plus price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin held at ~12.5%, the middle of the 11-14% guidance band and the FY23-26 average.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~9-10% of revenue (Pune, EVs, 26 launches) to 4%, close to depreciation; the FY23-FY26 average was 5.5%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Bayon and the compact EV take Hyundai's domestic share back toward 14% (FY24 level), exports return to 8-10% growth as the West Asia route reopens and the new Venue becomes a global product, Pune Phase 2 arrives on time and margins return to ~13.5%, the FY24-25 level.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The GST step-up fades into low single-digit industry growth; M&M, Tata, Maruti and Kia keep taking SUV share, so domestic volume grows ~4% a year; exports stay weak; commodity inflation persists and margins stay near FY27's 10-11%; the ₹45,000 cr capex plan is spent in full and depreciation rises faster.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Hyundai: every broker that discloses a method uses P/E on FY28E or Jun-28E EPS (24-30x). Multiple derived in tools/authoring/HYUNDAI.ctx.js (recently listed: own one-year-forward P/E median over the 12 months to 30-Sep-2026, times the auto-OEM sector's move against the same-window medians, nearest half-turn); written by HYUNDAI.mult.js.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Separates the car business from net cash. Multiple derived in HYUNDAI.ctx.js from the stock's own trailing EV/EBITDA over the same 12-month window and the same sector move, restated from trailing to Sep-28E EBITDA.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.9%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.
